sections.title: Describing how you do something
sections.content: To say HOW you do something, Hungarian usually turns an adjective into an adverb with -an/-en, matching vowel harmony — the general-purpose version of the -ul/-ül pattern you just used for languages. gyors ("fast") becomes gyorsan ("quickly"); lassú ("slow") becomes lassan ("slowly"); könnyű ("easy") becomes könnyen ("easily"); nehéz ("difficult"), which you already know, becomes nehezen ("with difficulty").

items.english: I have a hard time memorizing the grammar.

sections.content: Not every adverb follows -an/-en exactly — jó ("good") and rossz ("bad"), which you already know as jól and rosszul, are among the exceptions that take -ul/-ül instead. When in doubt, learn the adverb as its own word.
